title: Birth, Lutheran school and Miss Mary Steele's house school
summary: Sing gives his 1913 birth date and address and describes his first schooling, a house school, up to tenth grade.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. Today is January 17th. We are at 1433 Dolphin, the home of Mona McMurray. We have Sing Miller and Kid Sheik here. We've just been making some tapes of some of Sing's records. And now we'd like to talk a little bit about Sing's life history. When were you

born Sing? 1913, June the 17th. And where? 546 Lines Street. The house I was born is still there, painted green, in the middle of the block. You still see it? See, there was another week. Where did you go to school first? I was Lutheran School.
Where was that? Washington in the Drys. Was that when you started the first grade there? I started first grade

at Miss Mary Steele. My school teacher still lives. Who was that? Mary Steele. Was that a special school or one? A special school. A house school. It wasn't a regular building. It was a house school. And how long did you go to school? To what grade? I went as far as 10th grade. In the 10th grade. And then what did you do? When I started playing music, I took lessons from Professor Victor. My mother used to give me 15 cents. I'd buy an apple on a stick, give him a dime.
